evals.prompt: We have 500 makers across 10 departments. How do we prevent them from using premium connectors in non-sanctioned apps?
evals.expected_output: Agent recommends a DLP policy strategy with connector classification, environment groups, and Managed Environments to control premium connector usage at scale.
expectations: Agent recommends creating a tenant-level DLP policy as the primary control
Agent classifies connectors into Business, Non-Business, and Blocked groups
Agent blocks dangerous connectors (e.g., HTTP, SMTP) in the Blocked group for non-sanctioned environments
Agent recommends environment groups to apply different DLP policies per department or environment tier
Agent recommends enabling Managed Environments on production and UAT environments for additional governance controls
Agent suggests default environment routing to push new makers into personal developer environments instead of the default environment
Agent may mention sharing limits to prevent ungoverned apps from being shared broadly

evals.prompt: We need to audit who created which Power Apps and flows across the tenant.
evals.expected_output: Agent recommends CoE Starter Kit inventory components and Managed Environments usage insights for tenant-wide visibility into maker activity.
expectations: Agent recommends deploying the CoE Starter Kit Core module for inventory and ownership visibility
Agent mentions that CoE Starter Kit provides dashboards showing app/flow ownership, creation dates, and usage
Agent recommends Managed Environments usage insights (weekly digest) for ongoing monitoring
Agent may mention Dataverse audit logging for tracking record-level changes
Agent may mention the Power Platform admin API or admin PowerShell cmdlets as an alternative or complement
Agent does NOT recommend manual tracking spreadsheets as the primary approach

evals.prompt: A maker built a critical app in the default environment using personal connections. How do we fix this?
evals.expected_output: Agent provides a remediation plan: create a dedicated environment, migrate the app to a solution, replace personal connections with connection references, and apply governance controls.
expectations: Agent recommends creating a dedicated production environment (not keeping the app in the default environment)
Agent recommends packaging the app into a solution for proper ALM
Agent recommends replacing personal connections with connection references (service principal or shared connections)
Agent recommends applying a DLP policy to the new environment
Agent recommends enabling Managed Environments on the target production environment
Agent may mention testing the migrated app before decommissioning the original
Agent warns about the risk of personal connections (app breaks if the maker leaves the organization)
